Please act as a professional Verilog designer.

Implement a pulse bridge that converts a source-clock event into a one-cycle event in an independent destination clock domain.

Module name:
    prim_pulse_sync

Language:
    SystemVerilog

Clocks:
    clk_src_i: Rising-edge clock of the initiating source domain.
    clk_dst_i: Rising-edge clock of the receiving destination domain.

Resets:
    rst_src_ni: active low; asynchronous assertion.
    rst_dst_ni: active low; asynchronous assertion.

Input ports:
    clk_src_i: Rising-edge clock of the initiating source domain.
    rst_src_ni: Active-low asynchronous reset of source-domain state.
    src_pulse_i: Source-domain event indication, normally high for one source cycle.
    clk_dst_i: Rising-edge clock of the receiving destination domain.
    rst_dst_ni: Active-low asynchronous reset of destination-domain state.

Output ports:
    dst_pulse_o: One-destination-cycle event indication for each observed source toggle.

Parameters:
    None.

Behavior:
    - Toggle a source-domain level on each rising clk_src_i edge for which src_pulse_i is high.
    - Pass that level through a two-stage synchronizer clocked by clk_dst_i, then compare the synchronized value with its previous destination-cycle value using exclusive OR.
    - Drive dst_pulse_o for one destination-clock period after an observed toggle. Require source events to be separated enough for each transition to cross and be observed; this interface has no backpressure or event counter.
    - Asynchronously clear the source toggle with rst_src_ni and clear the destination synchronizer and history register with rst_dst_ni. Resetting only one side can itself appear as a toggle and generate a destination pulse, so coordinated reset is needed when that artifact is unacceptable.

Give me the complete code in one source file.
Do not include a testbench, explanation, markdown, vendor primitives,
or the reference implementation.

module prim_pulse_sync (
  // source clock domain
  input  logic clk_src_i,
  input  logic rst_src_ni,
  input  logic src_pulse_i,
  // destination clock domain
  input  logic clk_dst_i,
  input  logic rst_dst_ni,
  output logic dst_pulse_o
);

Implement a slow-to-fast data sampler that captures a stable slow-domain word when the fast domain observes a synchronized falling edge of the slow clock.

Module name:
    prim_sync_slow_fast

Language:
    SystemVerilog

Clocks:
    clk_slow_i: Slow-domain clock waveform sampled as data in the fast clock domain.
    clk_fast_i: Rising-edge sampling clock, substantially faster than clk_slow_i.

Resets:
    rst_fast_ni: active low; asynchronous assertion.

Input ports:
    clk_slow_i: Slow-domain clock waveform sampled as data in the fast clock domain.
    clk_fast_i: Rising-edge sampling clock, substantially faster than clk_slow_i.
    rst_fast_ni: Active-low asynchronous reset of all fast-domain state.
    wdata_i: Word originating in the slow domain, stable across the delayed fast-domain capture.

Output ports:
    rdata_o: Fast-domain registered copy of the most recently sampled word.

Parameters:
    Width: Number of bits sampled together from wdata_i into rdata_o; default 32.

Behavior:
    - Treat clk_slow_i as an asynchronous signal sampled by a two-stage synchronizer running on clk_fast_i; it does not directly clock a payload register in this module.
    - Remember the previous synchronized slow-clock level and recognize its high-to-low transition in the fast domain.
    - On a rising clk_fast_i edge with that falling-edge indication, capture the entire wdata_i word. Hold rdata_o unchanged on other fast-clock edges.
    - Require the slow producer to keep its word stable through the delayed sampling interval. Use a fast-to-slow frequency ratio of at least about ten to one as the intended operating assumption; this is not a general arbitrary-rate bus synchronizer.
    - Asynchronously clear the clock synchronizer, edge-history register, and sampled payload with the active-low rst_fast_ni. There is no separate slow-domain reset input.

Give me the complete code in one source file.
Do not include a testbench, explanation, markdown, vendor primitives,
or the reference implementation.

module prim_sync_slow_fast #(
  parameter int unsigned Width = 32
) (
  input  logic             clk_slow_i,
  input  logic             clk_fast_i,
  input  logic             rst_fast_ni,
  input  logic [Width-1:0] wdata_i,    // Slow domain
  output logic [Width-1:0] rdata_o     // Fast domain
);

  // Number of separately buffered output signals.
  // The buffer cells have a don't touch constraint

module prim_reg_cdc_arb #(
  parameter int DataWidth = 32,
  parameter logic [DataWidth-1:0] ResetVal = 32'h0,
  parameter bit DstWrReq = 0
) (
  input clk_src_i,
  input rst_src_ni,
  input clk_dst_i,
  input rst_dst_ni,
  // destination side acknowledging a software transaction
  output logic src_ack_o,
  // destination side requesting a source side update after
  // after hw update
  output logic src_update_o,
  // input request from prim_reg_cdc
  input dst_req_i,
  // output request to prim_subreg
  output logic dst_req_o,
  input dst_update_i,
  // ds allows us to sample the destination domain register
  // one cycle earlier instead of waiting for it to be reflected
  // in the qs.
  // This is important because a general use case is that interrupts
  // are captured alongside payloads from the destination domain into
  // the source domain. If we rely on `qs` only, then it is very likely
  // that the software observed value will be behind the interrupt
  // assertion.  If the destination clock is very slow, this can seem
  // an error on the part of the hardware.
  input [DataWidth-1:0] dst_ds_i,
  input [DataWidth-1:0] dst_qs_i,
  output logic [DataWidth-1:0] dst_qs_o
);
